newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end lower, consolidation seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end lower, consolidation seen.

text.p: Singapore shares ended lower in light trade on Friday as most players were sidelined ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
"Singapore is suffering from disinterest although we can see some players nibbling at some blue chips and selective counters," one dealer said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended 3.41 points down at 2,179.14. Turnover was light around 95 million shares, with losers outpacing gainers by 186 to 119.
Wong's Circuits dominated the actives, with over seven million shares. The share ended off US$0.01 at US$0.985.

Malaysia'S Berjaya Leisure, which saw 4.3 million shares traded, ended up Singapore $0.12 (US$0.09) at S$2.04. One dealer likened the counter to the Morning Glory flower: "We don't know whether it will hold."
Creative led gainers, rising S$0.60 to S$14.60 on 442,250 shares. Dealers said the rise was on the back of an upward revision in earnings for the company by some U.S. houses.
China Merchants fell HK$0.90 to HK$5.30 in sympathy with the Hong Kong bourse on 34,000 shares.
Dealers expect the STI index to stay range-bound at 2,150-2,190 in the near-term.
